==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|pleace||some English dialects: 18th–19th centuries; Scots: until the 17th century}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈpleɪ̯s/|[ˈpʰl̥eɪ̯s]|a=RP,GA,[[w:Standard Canadian English|Standard Canadian]]}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-to place.ogg|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-place.wav|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-place.ogg|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-place.wav|a=Southern England}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈpleːs/|[ˈpʰl̥eːs]|a=US,CA,[[w:Monophthongization|monophthongization]]}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈplæ̝ɪ̯s/|[ˈpʰl̥æ̝ɪ̯s]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪs|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|place}} * {{homophones|en|plaice}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleth₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|place}}, conflation of {{inh|en|ang|plæċe|t=place, an open space, street}} and {{der|en|fro|place|t=place, an open space}}, both from {{der|en|la|platēa|t=plaza, wide street}}, from {{der|en|grc|πλατεῖα}}, shortening of {{m|grc|[[πλατεῖα]] [[ὁδός]]|t=broad way}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleth₂-|t=to spread}}, extended form of {{m|ine-pro|*pleh₂-|t=flat}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|stōw}}, {{m|ang|stede}} (partially), and {{m|ang|-ern}}. Compare also {{noncog|en|pleck|t=plot of ground}}, {{noncog|fy|plak|t=place, spot, location}}, {{noncog|nl|plek|t=place, spot, patch}}. {{doublet|en|piatza|piazza|platz|plaza}}. In the etymological chain from {{m+|la|platēa}}, note {{m+|fro|place}}, which has multiple descendants — including {{cog|de|Platz}}, itself with many descendants (e.g., {{cog|ru|плац}}). Also note a more distant chain node {{cog|grc|πλατύς}}, whence {{cog|en|Plato}} and {{cog|en|plate}} (via Latin). ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|physical}} An [[area]]; [[somewhere]] within an [[area]]. ## An [[open]] [[space]], ''[[particularly]]'' a [[city]] [[square]], [[market]] [[square]], or [[courtyard]]. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|IV|iv|text=Ay, sir, the other squirrel was stolen from me by the hangman's boys in the market-'''place'''}} ## {{lb|en|often|in street names or addresses}} A street, sometimes but not always surrounding a public place, [[square]], or [[plaza]] of the same name. ##: {{ux|en|They live at Westminster '''Place'''.}} ## An [[inhabited]] [[area]]: a [[village]], [[town]], or [[city]]. ## [[any|Any]] [[area]] of the [[earth]]: a [[region]]. ##: {{ux|en|He is going back to his native '''place''' on vacation.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=From another point of view, it was a '''place''' without a soul. The well-to-do had hearts of stone; the rich were brutally bumptious; the Press, the Municipality, all the public men, were ridiculously, vaingloriously self-satisfied.}} ## The [[area]] [[one]] [[occupies]], ''[[particularly]]'' [[somewhere]] to [[sit]]. ##: {{ux|en|We asked the restaurant to give us a table with three '''places'''.}} ## The [[area]] where [[one]] [[live]]s: [[one]]'s [[home]], ''[[formerly]]'' {{label|en|chiefly}} [[country]] [[estate]]s and [[farm]]s. ##* {{RQ:Dickens Bleak House|text=My Lady Dedlock has been down at what she calls, in familiar conversation, her "'''place'''" in Lincolnshire.|2}} ##: {{ux|en|Do you want to come over to my '''place''' later?}} ## An [[area]] of the body, especially the [[skin]]. ##: {{ux|en|Which '''place''' hurts the most?}} ## {{label|en|dated|colloquial|euphemism}} An [[area]] to [[urinate]] and [[defecate]]: an [[outhouse]] or [[lavatory]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1901|author=John Stephen Farmer; et al|title=Slang and Its Analogues Past and Present|volume=V|page=220 |passage=''[[place|Place]]'',... (2) a [[jakes]], or [[house of ease]].}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1951|author=w:William Styron|title=w:Lie Down in Darkness|chapter=ii|page=59 |passage=‘I guess I'll take this opportunity to go to the [[place]]’...
‘She means the [[little girls room]].’}} ## {{label|en|obsolete}} An [[area]] to [[fight]]: a [[battlefield]] or the [[contested]] [[ground]] in a [[battle]]. # A [[location]] or [[position]] in [[space]]. #: {{ux|en|I'll check '''place'''s I think she might be.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|act=II|scene=v|passage=In that same '''place''' thou hast appointed me,
To-morrow truly will I meete with thee.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=2|passage=What '''place''' can be for us / Within heaven's bound?|year=1873}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=5|passage=When you're well enough off so's you don't have to fret about anything but your heft or your diseases you begin to get queer, I suppose. And the queerer the cure for those ailings the bigger the attraction. A '''place''' like the Right Livers' Rest was bound to draw freaks, same as molasses draws flies.}} # Proper or usual position. #: {{ux|en|A '''place''' for everything, and everything in its '''place'''.}} # A [[particular]] [[location]] in a [[book]] or [[document]], ''[[particularly]]'' the [[current]] [[location]] of a [[reader]] #: {{ux|en|I lost my '''place''' when you interrupted me.}} # {{label|en|obsolete}} A [[passage]] or [[extract]] from a [[book]] or [[document]]. # {{label|en|obsolete|rhetoric}} A [[topic]]. # A [[state of mind]]. #: {{ux|en|I'm in a strange '''place''' at the moment.}} # {{label|en|chess|obsolete}} A [[chess]] [[position]]; a [[square]] of the [[chessboard]]. # {{lb|en|social}} A [[responsibility]] or [[position]] in an [[organization]]. ## A [[role]] or [[purpose]]; a [[station]]. ##: {{ux|en|It is really not my '''place''' to say what is right and wrong in this case.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|II|v|passage=I know my '''place''' as I would they should do theirs.}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Measure|I|i |passage=''Escalus''.Esc.I shall desire you, Sir, to giue me leaue
